feeds.feed: Initial claims, continued claims, insured unemployment rate
feeds.source: Department of Labor (the UI claims news release; ALFRED vintages after it)
feeds.every: Weekly - Thursday 8:30 AM ET (Wednesday before a Thursday holiday)
feeds.backup: the states' ETA 539 weekly file with the Bureau's seasonal factors (s2/claims_substitute.py, exact where tested; collection 329)
feeds.format_check: q41 feed checks; the claims loader asserts the release week columns (45)

feeds.feed: State insured unemployment rates (the breadth object)
feeds.source: Department of Labor (page 8 of the weekly release; the advance state table of the release PDF while the archive catches up)
feeds.every: Weekly - Thursday 8:30 AM ET, one week behind initial claims
feeds.backup: the advance state table of the weekly release PDF while the archive catches up
feeds.format_check: the page-8 parse validated against the advance table

feeds.feed: Unemployment rate, factory hours, nondurable employment
feeds.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation
feeds.every: Monthly - usually the first Friday, 8:30 AM ET
feeds.backup: the Chicago Fed real-time unemployment forecast; ADP private payrolls (LSEG first prints) - declared, not automated
feeds.format_check: q41: the tile and the readings recomputed from the fetched files

feeds.every: Monthly - about five weeks after the month, 10:00 AM ET
feeds.backup: the Indeed Hiring Lab postings index, at most two months (s2/vacancy_bridge.py; collection 330)
feeds.format_check: walk39 asserts the vacancy first prints are not stale (>150 rows, within 8 months)

feeds.backup: building permits beside starts (the pair reads either); the Census calendar

feeds.feed: Commercial paper and three-month bill rates (the spread)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve, H.15 selected interest rates
feeds.every: Daily - the Board posts the H.15 every business day at 4:15 PM ET, carrying the previous business day's rates (the bill rate is a weekly series)
feeds.backup: FRED DCPN30, DCPF1M and DTB3 (the Federal Reserve is not shut in a shutdown)
feeds.format_check: q41: the paper rates and their last printed day

feeds.feed: S&P 500 daily close (the market gate of the sudden stop, the activity opener and the concurrence branch, and a confirmation of the claims closer)
feeds.source: Yahoo Finance close at the 5:05 PM ET run, corrected to the official close on FRED (SP500), which FRED posts the same evening, about 8 PM ET
feeds.every: Every trading day - read at the 5:05 PM ET run
feeds.backup: the official FRED SP500 close when the chart feed fails (two independent quotes)
feeds.format_check: q41: reading matches the readings table; two sources compared

feeds.feed: Industrial production, as published (the activity opener)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve, G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (each month as first published: ALFRED vintages)
feeds.backup: the FRED current file of INDPRO (flagged: revised values), then the G.17 release text
feeds.format_check: activity_opener.py: the vintage history appended and checked

feeds.feed: Federal funds target range, upper limit (the activity opener's tightening condition)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve, FOMC statement (FRED DFEDTARU, the daily series)
feeds.every: Daily - FRED posts the series every day, weekends included, at about 8:01 AM ET; it moves only at an FOMC decision (eight scheduled meetings a year, the statement at 2:00 PM ET), carried by the next morning's post
feeds.backup: the FOMC statement on federalreserve.gov (the rate carried from the last reading until then)
feeds.format_check: activity_opener.py: the FOMC calendar end alert (watchdog)

feeds.feed: State continued weeks claimed, ETA 539 (the activity opener's breadth gate)
feeds.source: Department of Labor, ETA 539 weekly state claims (continued weeks claimed, by state), over state payroll employment (BLS, from FRED)
feeds.every: Monthly - each month is read 21 days after it ends, from the Department's weekly file
feeds.backup: the ETA 5159 monthly report (slower), then the last month read

feeds.feed: State unemployment rates, all 51 (the second opener)
feeds.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Local Area Unemployment Statistics, as first printed (ALFRED initial releases)
feeds.every: Monthly - with the State Employment and Unemployment release, about three weeks after the month, 10:00 AM ET
feeds.backup: the states' ETA 539 insured-rate acceleration, at most two months (collection 336)
feeds.format_check: state_breadth.py: 45-state coverage guard; q41 v3.72 checks

feeds.feed: Real GDP (the damage grade's output dimension)
feeds.source: Bureau of Economic Analysis, Gross Domestic Product news release (FRED GDPC1, the latest vintage)
feeds.every: Quarterly - the advance estimate about four weeks after the quarter, revised in each of the next two months; 8:30 AM ET
feeds.backup: GDPNow for the unprinted quarter; the BEA release text
feeds.format_check: damage_dimensions.py: the vintage table read by column name; q41 v3.73 checks

feeds.feed: GDPNow (the output dimension's bridge for the quarter not yet printed)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, GDPNow (FRED GDPNOW, every update as a vintage)
feeds.every: Several times a month, on the days of the releases it reads (FRED carries each update between about 10:30 AM and 1 PM ET); the Atlanta Fed posts its schedule
feeds.backup: the Atlanta Fed page; the last printed quarter carried
feeds.format_check: the vintage appender names each vintage by its FRED date

feeds.feed: Sahm rule, real time (the comparator on the speed panel)
feeds.every: Monthly - FRED posts it on the morning of the employment report, after the Bureau's 8:30 AM ET release
feeds.backup: computed from the unemployment rate first prints if FRED SAHMREALTIME lapses

feeds.feed: Search week: Google searches for "unemployment" (the sudden stop's second labour datum)
feeds.source: Google Trends, United States, daily index stitched onto one scale and extended each day
feeds.every: Daily - a day's index is complete when the day ends in UTC (8 PM ET in summer, 7 PM in winter), weekends included; read at every weekday close
feeds.backup: the claims week alone at any cell looser than (35, 20) (E34c); a second search source is not yet declared (R2)
feeds.format_check: the collector's anchored window and the R2 shape guard (108/scripts/trends_live.py: a re-fetched window whose overlap deviates over 15 per cent is not appended; pull_log.csv)

feeds.feed: Search week: Google searches for "layoffs" (the sudden stop's second labour datum)
feeds.source: Google Trends, United States, daily index stitched onto one scale and extended each day
feeds.every: Daily - a day's index is complete when the day ends in UTC (8 PM ET in summer, 7 PM in winter), weekends included; read at every weekday close
feeds.backup: the claims week alone at any cell looser than (35, 20) (E34c); a second search source is not yet declared (R2)
feeds.format_check: the collector's anchored window and the R2 shape guard (108/scripts/trends_live.py: a re-fetched window whose overlap deviates over 15 per cent is not appended; pull_log.csv)

feeds.feed: Search week: Google searches for "laid off" (the sudden stop's second labour datum)
feeds.source: Google Trends, United States, daily index stitched onto one scale and extended each day
feeds.every: Daily - a day's index is complete when the day ends in UTC (8 PM ET in summer, 7 PM in winter), weekends included; read at every weekday close
feeds.backup: the claims week alone at any cell looser than (35, 20) (E34c); a second search source is not yet declared (R2)
feeds.format_check: the collector's anchored window and the R2 shape guard (108/scripts/trends_live.py: a re-fetched window whose overlap deviates over 15 per cent is not appended; pull_log.csv)
